evidence: Parent AC2: 'Every surviving operation keeps its --output json bytes, its exit codes, and its library and MCP names. Checked by ... an unchanged parity manifest.'

fea5 ACs list only: route_for None, STORE_ROUTES validates, per-member init policy, compact-sweep + generators + exit-code + probe green, 'JSON output of every member is byte-identical to its pre-move golden', make verify. No mention of mcp_library_parity_manifest.json or library/MCP names.
4183 AC: 'Library and MCP names untouched: git diff --exit-code tests/unit/mcp_library_parity_manifest.json is clean' — present only in the ticket-merges story.

fea5 renames handlers (compact -> compact_dispatch_cli, tracker-maintenance -> maintenance member name) and moves verbs under store, so the library/MCP-name invariant for storage ops is a real surface the parent requires to be checked.
container pairing: parent + 2183-fa68-d48f-42fe/3e7a-d8ef-ce56-4eb7/4183-cd0a-8407-49fd/fea5-698b-d585-40c4
findings.finding: Parent AC2 requires 'its library and MCP names' to be preserved for every surviving operation, checked by 'an unchanged parity manifest', but only the merges story (4183) pins the parity manifest ('git diff --exit-code tests/unit/mcp_library_parity_manifest.json is clean'). The store story (fea5) covers the nine storage members' surviving ops and has NO parity-manifest / library-MCP-name assertion in its acceptance criteria — it asserts only JSON byte-identity, per-member init policy, and route validation. No sibling in the roster pins library/MCP-name invariance for the store members.
scenarios: A store-member move or handler rename inadvertently changes a library or MCP name/mapping for a storage op; because fea5 never diffs the parity manifest, nothing in the store story's gate catches it, and the completion verifier for parent AC2 (which names the unchanged parity manifest) has no child check backing the storage half.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to fea5's acceptance criteria: 'Library and MCP names untouched: git diff --exit-code tests/unit/mcp_library_parity_manifest.json is clean.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the docs story (3e7a) and/or merges story (4183) explicitly responsible for the 5 historical `_REMOVED_SPELLINGS` entries — verify each historical hint's replacement is still a live command and no historical spelling appears on an ungated surface — so the held-out test's dict-wide scan (2183) has no owned-by-none remainder.
evidence: 4183 Approach (1): 'replace the three frozensets at :32-38 with one dict _REMOVED_SPELLINGS: dict[str, str] (5 historical entries, replacements per docs/exit-codes.md:107-108, plus the 12)'.

2183 Approach (a): 'for every key in _help_route._REMOVED_SPELLINGS: ... the hint's first token after `rebar ` is a live top-level route' and (b) a scan for `rebar <old>` — i.e. parametrized over the full dict including the 5 historical keys.
3e7a Testing grep enumerates only the 20 new removals: 'rebar (exists|format|check-ac|...|export|import)'; the 5 historical spellings are not in that alternation nor in 3e7a's edit list.
container pairing: parent + 2183-fa68-d48f-42fe/3e7a-d8ef-ce56-4eb7/4183-cd0a-8407-49fd/fea5-698b-d585-40c4
findings.finding: Residual-reference / consumer-impact: the merges story (4183) folds the old `format` verb into `resolve --display` and the held-out drift test (2183) scans for `rebar <old>` for every key in `_REMOVED_SPELLINGS`, but `_REMOVED_SPELLINGS` includes 5 pre-existing historical entries (per 4183 Approach: 'replace the three frozensets ... with one dict ... (5 historical entries ... plus the 12)'). The held-out story's scan is parametrized over the whole dict and will therefore assert that the 5 historical spellings also never appear on any teaching surface and that each historical hint's replacement is a live command. Neither the docs story (3e7a) grep nor the docs story's edit list covers those 5 historical spellings — the docs grep enumerates only the 20 newly-removed verbs. If any historical spelling's replacement text is stale or appears in docs, the held-out test (AC4) can go red with nothing in the docs story (AC3) having addressed it.
scenarios: A historical removed spelling's replacement in the inherited frozensets points at a now-nonexistent command, or a historical spelling still appears in a doc the docs story did not touch; the held-out test (2183) fails on a key the docs story (3e7a) was never scoped to clean.
findings.suggested_fix: In 4183, add an AC that the 5 inherited historical hints resolve to live commands when migrated into the dict; and extend 3e7a's grep alternation (or allowlist rationale) to cover the 5 historical spellings so the held-out scan domain is fully owned.

findings.finding: The plan states three different counts for how many verbs are removed and they do not reconcile: the title promises '72 verbs to 54' (18 net removed), the Context says 'Twenty of them duplicate', and the Child decomposition sums to 21 (twelve ticket verbs + nine storage verbs). An implementer cannot tell whether 18, 20, or 21 spellings must be removed and hinted, which directly affects criterion 1's parametrized dispatch test over the hint registry.
findings.suggested_fix: State the exact removed-spelling list once (the mapping table in the first comment) and make the title/net-count, the 'Twenty' phrasing, and the child scopes all derive from it — e.g. clarify that merging three check verbs into one removes 2 net verbs, so removed-names != net-verb-reduction, and give both numbers explicitly.

4183 title: 'Merge twelve ticket verbs'; Context: 'Twelve near-duplicate ticket verbs (`exists`/`format`, `check-ac`/`clarity-check`/`quality-check`, `tag`/`untag`, `get-file-impact`/`get-verify-commands`, `list-descendants`, `session-logs`)' — that parenthetical enumerates 11.

container pairing: parent + 2183-fa68-d48f-42fe/3e7a-d8ef-ce56-4eb7/4183-cd0a-8407-49fd/fea5-698b-d585-40c4
findings.finding: The merges story (4183) repeatedly refers to 'twelve ticket verbs' / 'all 12' (title, Context, Approach, AC1), but its own enumerated set and the parent epic's mapping table list only ELEVEN ticket spellings (exists, format, check-ac, clarity-check, quality-check, tag, untag, get-file-impact, get-verify-commands, list-descendants, session-logs). The parent decomposition likewise says 'criterion 1 for the twelve ticket verbs' while the parent's own census and mapping table count 11 ticket + 9 storage = 20. The '12' appears to double-count (e.g. both compact and compact-all, or treating check-ac/clarity-check/quality-check as collapsing to one new 'check' plus an extra). The parametrized dispatch test iterating `_REMOVED_SPELLINGS` will enumerate whatever is actually in the dict, so the discrepancy is a labeling inconsistency, not a routing gap — but it is a conflicting-assumption/consistency defect between the child and the parent.
scenarios: A reviewer or implementer treats '12' as authoritative and expects a 12th ticket removed-spelling that the mapping table does not define, or the dispatch test's expected count is hard-coded to 12 and fails against an 11-entry ticket slice of the dict.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'twelve'/'all 12' with 'eleven'/'all 11' throughout 4183 and the parent decomposition line, matching the 11-row ticket slice of the epic mapping table (total still 20 removed).
